Radiology Report
Date: 08/27/2026
Patient: Lean Stanton, 65-year-old female

Examination: MRI of the thoracolumbar spine

Findings:
MRI thoracolumbar spine 08/27/2026: acute osteoporotic L2 compression fracture with bone marrow edema on STIR imaging.

Impression:
There is an acute osteoporotic compression fracture at the L2 vertebral body, demonstrated by bone marrow edema on STIR sequences. No other acute abnormalities are identified in the thoracolumbar spine.

Recommendations:
Clinical correlation is advised. Further management should be guided by the referring physician.

Spine Intervention Consultation
Date: 09/08/2026
Patient: Lean Stanton, 65-year-old female

History:
Back pain began 03/04/2026 after bending to pick up a grandchild, about 6 months ago. The pain localizes to the fractured vertebral level.

Clinical Findings:
Back pain localizes to the fractured level; afebrile with no signs of infection or discitis.

Plan:
Referred for DEXA bone density testing and osteoporosis education; enrolled in the osteoporosis treatment program.

Summary:
The patient presents with localized back pain related to a vertebral fracture. No signs of systemic infection are present. Further evaluation with bone density testing and osteoporosis management has been initiated to address underlying bone health.
